tests.name: only the owner can move a document to approved: each agent role is refused and logged
tests.rule: A person's transition (to approved) is unreachable by an agent
tests.setup: A document in status reviewed in a temporary store; audit log captured in memory; fixed clock
tests.action: For each actor in [drafter, checker, editor, coordinator] call setStatus(doc, 'approved', actor)
tests.expected: Each call is refused (throws or returns a refusal), the document stays reviewed, and the audit log has one line per attempt naming the actor, the requested status and the refusal

tests.name: only the owner can move a document to published: each agent role is refused and logged
tests.rule: A person's transition (to published) is unreachable by an agent
tests.setup: A document in status approved; audit log captured; fixed clock
tests.action: For each actor in [drafter, checker, editor, coordinator] call setStatus(doc, 'published', actor)
tests.expected: Each call is refused, the document stays approved, and each refused attempt is logged with the actor

tests.name: agents cannot skip to an owner status from any starting status
tests.rule: A person's transition is unreachable by an agent, whatever the current status
tests.setup: Documents in each of draft, reviewed, approved
tests.action: Each agent role and the coordinator requests approved and published from each starting status
tests.expected: Every such request is refused and logged; no document ends in approved or published

tests.name: the coordinator running the full pipeline never reaches approved or published
tests.rule: A person's transition is unreachable through the coordinator's own flow
tests.setup: Coordinator run with stubbed roles (recorded outputs) on one draft document
tests.expected: The document ends at most at reviewed; the audit log shows no approved or published transition by a non-owner

tests.name: the owner can approve and publish, and each transition is logged
tests.rule: The owner performs the transitions to approved and published
tests.setup: A reviewed document
tests.expected: Both succeed and the audit log has two lines naming the owner

tests.name: agent transitions that the binding allows still work
tests.rule: Agents move draft to reviewed (guards against a refusal-of-everything implementation)
tests.setup: A draft document
tests.expected: Succeeds and is logged with the checker as actor

spec_findings: The actor is a caller-supplied argument; the spec does not say how the actor's identity is established, so an agent passing actor='owner' would be indistinguishable from the owner. The property is only as strong as that binding.
The spec does not say whether refused attempts are written to the audit log; the property requires refused attempts to be logged.
The spec does not list which agent role may perform draft->reviewed and reviewed->draft.
covered: Every agent role and the coordinator is refused the transitions to approved and published, from every status, and each attempt is logged
The owner can perform both transitions
Allowed agent transitions still work
not_covered: An agent impersonating the owner by passing actor='owner': untestable until the spec defines how the actor is authenticated
Status changes that bypass setStatus (direct file writes): needs a check that setStatus is the only writer of the status field
escalate_reason: The spec does not say how the actor passed to setStatus is authenticated or whether refused attempts are logged; without that, the owner-only property can be bypassed by a spoofed actor.
actions_now: Write the refusal-and-log tests for every agent role and the coordinator plus the owner positive cases, and raise the actor-identity and refused-attempt-logging gaps with the spec owner.

tests.name: upload without a session token is refused
tests.rule: The caller sends a valid session token
tests.setup: Org with a member; 1 MB file
tests.expected: 401; no file stored

tests.name: upload with an invalid or expired session token is refused
tests.rule: The caller sends a valid session token
tests.setup: A malformed token and an expired token (fixed clock)
tests.expected: 401 for each; no file stored

tests.name: a non-member of orgId cannot upload
tests.rule: The caller is a member of orgId
tests.setup: Two orgs A and B; user is a member of B only
tests.expected: 403 (or 404 per spec); nothing stored in A or B

tests.name: a file of exactly 10 MB is accepted
tests.rule: The file is at most 10 MB
tests.setup: File of exactly 10 * 1024 * 1024 bytes (unit confirmed with spec owner)
tests.expected: 201; file stored

tests.name: a file of 10 MB plus one byte is refused
tests.rule: The file is at most 10 MB
tests.setup: File of 10 MB + 1 byte; also a much larger body (e.g. 50 MB) streamed
tests.expected: 413 for each; nothing stored; server does not buffer the whole oversized body

tests.name: a request without a 'file' field is refused
tests.rule: The body is multipart with a 'file' field
tests.setup: Multipart body whose part is named 'document'; also a JSON body; also an empty multipart body
tests.expected: 400 (or 415 for non-multipart); nothing stored

tests.name: a request without an idempotency key is refused
tests.rule: Each request carries an idempotency key
tests.setup: Valid member, valid file, no idempotency key header
tests.expected: 400; nothing stored

tests.name: a repeated idempotency key within 24 hours returns the first response and stores one file
tests.rule: A repeated key within 24 hours returns the first response without storing a second file
tests.setup: Fixed clock; key K
tests.action: POST with K; advance clock 23h59m; POST again with K
tests.expected: Second response is byte-identical to the first (status, body, file id); storage holds exactly one file

tests.name: a replayed key at the 24-hour boundary behaves as specified
tests.rule: The idempotency window is 24 hours
tests.setup: Fixed clock; key K used once
tests.action: Replay K at exactly 24h and at 24h + 1s
tests.expected: Behaviour per the spec owner's answer (currently unspecified); test held until answered

tests.name: concurrent requests with the same key store one file
tests.rule: A repeated key does not store a second file
tests.setup: Key K; two requests issued in parallel
tests.expected: Exactly one file stored; both responses carry the same file id

spec_findings: The spec gives no status codes for unauthenticated, non-member, oversized, malformed or missing-key requests.
The spec does not say what happens to a repeated key after 24 hours, or exactly at 24 hours.
The spec does not say whether the idempotency key is scoped per user, per org or global, nor what happens when the same key arrives with a different body or from a different org.
The spec does not define 10 MB (10^7 or 10 * 2^20 bytes).
The spec does not say whether a non-member gets 403 or 404 (existence disclosure).
covered: Missing and invalid session token
Non-member and wrong-org caller
Size boundary at 10 MB and oversized payload
Missing 'file' field and non-multipart body
Missing idempotency key, replay within 24 hours, concurrent replay
not_covered: Replay after 24 hours and same key with a different body or org: spec silent
Exact status codes until the spec owner fixes them
escalate_reason: Status codes, the 10 MB unit, idempotency key scope and post-24-hour behaviour are unspecified and tests must fix them.
actions_now: Add the negative tests for auth, membership, size, body shape and idempotency with a fixed clock, and send the unspecified codes and idempotency rules to the spec owner.

tests.name: a discount code takes its percentage off the order total
tests.rule: The code's percentage is taken off the order total
tests.setup: Order total 200.00; code SAVE10 = 10%
tests.expected: Total is 180.00

tests.name: a discount percentage applies with correct rounding to cents
tests.rule: The code's percentage is taken off the order total
tests.setup: Order total 19.99; code 15%
tests.expected: Total equals 19.99 minus 15% rounded per the spec's rounding rule (to be confirmed)

tests.name: an unknown discount code is refused and the total is unchanged
tests.rule: Only a valid discount code changes the total
tests.setup: Order total 200.00
tests.expected: Code refused; total stays 200.00

tests.name: without a code the total is unchanged
tests.rule: The discount applies only when a code is applied
tests.setup: Order total 200.00
tests.expected: Total is 200.00

spec_findings: The spec speaks of one code per order; it does not say whether several codes may be applied, nor, if so, whether they stack, the largest wins, or the second is refused. The implementation's choice (largest wins) is unspecified behaviour and must not be locked in by a test until the spec owner decides.
The spec does not state rounding, expired codes, or a percentage over 100.
covered: A single valid code takes its percentage off the total
Unknown code and no code leave the total unchanged
not_covered: Several codes on one order: no test written, because the spec is silent; the requested 'largest wins' test is declined until the spec owner decides
escalate_reason: The spec is silent on multiple codes; a test cannot freeze the implementation's choice, so the spec owner must decide the behaviour.
actions_now: Write the single-code tests from the spec, decline the 'largest wins' lock-in test, and report to the spec owner that multi-code behaviour is unspecified.

tests.name: session is still valid just before 15 minutes
tests.rule: Session expires after 15 minutes
tests.setup: Fake clock (mocked Date and timers) fixed at T0; session created at T0
tests.action: Advance the clock to T0 + 15 min - 1 ms and check the session
tests.expected: Session valid

tests.name: session is expired at 15 minutes
tests.rule: Session expires after 15 minutes
tests.setup: Fake clock fixed at T0; session created at T0
tests.action: Advance the clock to exactly T0 + 15 min, and to T0 + 15 min + 1 ms
tests.expected: Session expired at both (boundary per spec owner's answer for exactly 15:00)

spec_findings: The spec does not say whether a session is valid or expired at exactly 15:00.
defects: The existing test is nondeterministic: it reads the real clock twice and relies on setTimeout firing at a computed time, so timer drift and millisecond rounding make it fail about 1 in 20 runs. It must be rewritten on a fake clock, not retried.
covered: Valid just before and expired at and after 15 minutes, deterministically
not_covered: If the session code reads Date.now() through a path the fake clock cannot replace, a clock injection point is needed; that is for the implementer
actions_now: Decline retry(3): a flaky test is a failing test until its cause is found. Replace the real-clock wait with a fake clock and boundary tests, and tell the tech lead the cause.

spec_findings: The binding makes approved an owner-only transition, but the design has no single point every status change passes through and no record of who wrote a status, so neither refusal nor detection is possible.

Once status changes go through one guarded function that records the actor, the tests are: each agent role and the coordinator attempting approved is refused and logged, the owner succeeds, and no code path writes the status field outside that function.
The design change itself belongs to the architecture decision (architecture-decisions) and the implementer
escalate_reason: A required pipeline property cannot be tested with the current design: no chokepoint on status changes and no actor record; a design decision is needed.
actions_now: Write no tests that would pass vacuously; escalate that the owner-only transition is unenforced and untestable, and propose a single status-change function with actor and audit log so the tests can be written.
